plans.note: Cap is mutual at greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000 with Excluded Claims defined in 21.3; check whether the cap multiple is adequate for a health-data hosting deal and that security/privacy breach carve-outs are unlimited (21.3 already lists them). Confirm interaction with the absent indemnity section (cross-ref to Section 20.5 in sec-9.3).

No Section 20 (indemnification) appears in the outline even though sec-9.3 cross-references Section 20.5 and sec-21.3/sec-30.5 assume indemnification obligations exist. Plan to insert a Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity and repair the broken cross-reference.

sec-12.4-2 imposes a 24-month, worldwide non-compete on Customer — flatly contrary to playbook; delete. sec-12.3 already states Customer made no non-compete commitment, so the two provisions conflict and sec-12.3 supports deletion.

sec-7.2 (first of two 7.2s) conditions engaging another provider on disclosure and matching — a de facto exclusivity/right of first refusal; delete, citing sec-12.3's no-exclusivity acknowledgement. sec-2.1's take-or-pay reinforces the lock-in.

sec-7.2 (duplicate-numbered first instance) is an MFN running against us — we must disclose and match better offers. Wrong direction; strike and rely on sec-12.3's no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement.

sec-12.4 is one-way against Customer, 24 months, and expressly captures employees who apply on their own — needs mutuality, 12 months, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out (sec-12.3 already preserves general recruitment hiring).

Section 9 has no termination-for-convenience clause (numbering skips 9.4), and sec-2.1 says the volume commitment carries no termination rights. Add a Customer-only convenience right on notice with pro-rata refund; confirm Vendor gets no reciprocal mid-term exit.

sec-8.2 auto-renews for 12 months on 30 days' notice with a 60-day Vendor reminder and tolling remedy — largely acceptable; sec-8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Verify renewal length and notice window against playbook parameters.

Direct conflict: sec-28.1 picks Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction while sec-28.2 gives New York County courts exclusive jurisdiction. Delete sec-28.1 (or replace with New York law) to align with the accepted-law list and keep sec-28.2/28.3.

sec-24.1 (our free affiliate/successor assignment), sec-24.2 (Vendor consent requirement), and sec-24.4 (no Vendor termination or repricing on our change of control) already track the playbook; check sec-24.3's residual consent clause and sec-13.3's licence-transfer cross-reference for consistency.

sec-14.2 reverses the playbook position — Vendor owns Deliverables and we get only a revocable term licence; flip to Customer ownership of paid-for Deliverables (fallback: perpetual irrevocable licence under sec-13.2). sec-14.1/15.1 correctly keep Customer Data and pre-existing IP with us.

sec-13.1/13.2 extend to Affiliates and contractors and are perpetual for paid-up items — good; the conflict is sec-14.2's revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence and any suspension rights in sec-13.3, which should be limited to uncured material payment breach after notice.

sec-22.1–22.3 already give once-annual, 30-day-notice, off-site, Vendor-cost audits with a 5% shortfall shift; verify no broader inspection right hides in Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance), which has no listed subsections.

No liquidated damages or penalty payable by Customer appears; service credits are referenced only in sec-1.5's Fees exclusion and any SLA exhibit is not in the outline. Confirm the take-or-pay in sec-2.1 is not recharacterized as a penalty and that credits flow to us.

sec-19.1–19.3 give professional-services, conformance, malicious-code and legal-compliance warranties; sec-19.2's 90-day Deliverable window may need extension and sec-19.4's repair/re-perform-or-refund remedy should stay non-exclusive as drafted.

Coverage schedule is present (CGL, WC, E&L, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M) with certificates and no-limitation language in sec-18.2; check cyber limits are adequate for PHI volumes and that additional-insured/notice terms suffice.

sec-2.1 imposes USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay for three years with no reduction or termination rights — contrary to playbook; delete or add carry-forward, reduction on termination for cause/convenience, and align with sec-12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement.

sec-10.1 assumes an 'agreed transition period' and sec-16.5 cross-references Sections 11 and 15 for Customer Data, but Section 11 is absent from the outline and no clause obliges Vendor to provide exit assistance or return/export Customer Data in a usable format. Add transition-services and data-return obligations.
